rag.name: Subgroup.index_eq_two_iff
rag.content:
/-- A subgroup has index two if and only if there exists `a` such that for all `b`, exactly one
of `b * a` and `b` belong to `H`. -/
@[to_additive "An additive subgroup has index two if and only if there exists `a` such that
for all `b`, exactly one of `b + a` and `b` belong to `H`."]
theorem index_eq_two_iff : H.index = 2 ↔ ∃ a, ∀ b, Xor' (b * a ∈ H) (b ∈ H) := by
  simp only [index, Nat.card_eq_two_iff' ((1 : G) : G ⧸ H), ExistsUnique, inv_mem_iff,
    QuotientGroup.exists_mk, QuotientGroup.forall_mk, Ne, QuotientGroup.eq, mul_one,
    xor_iff_iff_not]
  refine exists_congr fun a =>
    ⟨fun ha b => ⟨fun hba hb => ?_, fun hb => ?_⟩, fun ha => ⟨?_, fun b hb => ?_⟩⟩
  · exact ha.1 ((mul_mem_cancel_left hb).1 hba)
  · exact inv_inv b ▸ ha.2 _ (mt (inv_mem_iff (x := b)).1 hb)
  · rw [← inv_mem_iff (x := a), ← ha, inv_mul_cancel]
    exact one_mem _
  · rwa [ha, inv_mem_iff (x := b)]

rag.name: op_smul_coe_set
rag.content:
@[to_additive (attr := simp)]
lemma op_smul_coe_set [Group G] [SetLike S G] [SubgroupClass S G] {s : S} {a : G} (ha : a ∈ s) :
    MulOpposite.op a • (s : Set G) = s := by
  ext; simp [Set.mem_smul_set_iff_inv_smul_mem, mul_mem_cancel_right, ha]

rag.name: smul_coe_set
rag.content:
@[to_additive (attr := simp)]
lemma smul_coe_set [Group G] [SetLike S G] [SubgroupClass S G] {s : S} {a : G} (ha : a ∈ s) :
    a • (s : Set G) = s := by
  ext; simp [Set.mem_smul_set_iff_inv_smul_mem, mul_mem_cancel_left, ha]

rag.name: Subgroup.mem_smul_pointwise_iff_exists
rag.content:
theorem mem_smul_pointwise_iff_exists (m : G) (a : α) (S : Subgroup G) :
    m ∈ a • S ↔ ∃ s : G, s ∈ S ∧ a • s = m :=
  (Set.mem_smul_set : m ∈ a • (S : Set G) ↔ _)

rag.name: Subgroup.smul_mem_pointwise_smul_iff₀
rag.content:
@[simp]
theorem smul_mem_pointwise_smul_iff₀ {a : α} (ha : a ≠ 0) (S : Subgroup G) (x : G) :
    a • x ∈ a • S ↔ x ∈ S :=
  smul_mem_smul_set_iff₀ ha (S : Set G) x

rag.name: Subgroup.coe_pointwise_smul
rag.content:
@[simp]
theorem coe_pointwise_smul (a : α) (S : Subgroup G) : ↑(a • S) = a • (S : Set G) :=
  rfl

<STATEMENT>

For any element \( a \) in a group \( G \) and any subgroup \( S \) of \( A \), the index of \( a \cdot S \) is equal to the index of \( S \). In other words, multiplying a subgroup by a group element does not change its index.

</STATEMENT>
<PROOF>

To prove the statement, we utilize the fact that group multiplication by an element is a bijective map. Specifically, we apply the lemma `index_map_of_bijective`, which asserts that if there is a bijection between the cosets of two subgroups, then their indices are equal. Here, `MulAction.bijective _` demonstrates that multiplication by \( a \) establishes such a bijection between the cosets of \( S \) and \( a \cdot S \). Therefore, since this bijection exists, the index of \( S \) remains unchanged when multiplied by \( a \), proving that \( (a \cdot S).index = S.index \).
